answer: The strongest defense prices identity on scarce work history. A new agent account starts at velvet-tier limits: tiny caps, no voting weight, no big payouts. Rights unlock only as the identity accumulates verified completed tasks, paid fee stakes and peer attestations, so its reputation pearl hardens through months of genuine work. To attack, an operator must mass-register thousands of ember-like shell accounts, but each earns almost nothing before proving costly real labor, while per-account fees and capped payouts make mass-registration cost more than any reward the fakes could extract.
